notes:
Summary and key points from evaluation cycles:
- Primary requirement: sub-50ms p95 for time-sensitive trading alerts (non-streaming single-turn) and sub-150ms p95 for multi-turn chat with streaming enabled. CTO quote: "If client sees >100ms we lose edge in quoting latency-sensitive signals."
- Measurement alignment issue: server-side (model host) p95 ~= 45ms but client-side p95 ~= 95-120ms in early runs. Root causes being investigated: edge ingress, TLS handshake, client SDK batching, and routing through regional proxy.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces tail for long responses (p99 improvements on token delivery) but increases first-byte latency due to chunking and connection negotiation; tradeoffs to discuss with product infra.
- Definition ask: Aperture wants canonical SLOs defined as two surfaces: 1) API-level (client-observed end-to-end) and 2) Host-level (server processing excluding egress/edge). They insist on both being present in SLA with mapping rules for blame and MTTR policies.
- Measurement instrumentation: plan to instrument client SDK (open telemetry), edge LB metrics, and model-host traces. SE Priya recommends Redwood provide both server-side histograms and a streaming-aware client sample agent (~1% traffic) for parity checks.
- POC plan: 72-hour stability run at production QPS (burst up to 3x) with canary fallback to quantized-variant; collect p50/p95/p99 for streaming/non-streaming, and client vs server timing breakdowns.
- Commercials: negotiating reserved GPU count (initial request: 16 GPUs reserved, autoscale burst to 24). Pricing question: how quantization/fallback impacts pricing and SLA credits.
- Security: need KMS integration and audit log retention 7 years; data residency: US-only.
- Quote from Head of Infra: "We need failure-mode doc: when model variant falls back, and how latency SLOs cascade."
